## Download

- **Mac** (Apple silicon or Intel, macOS 11 or later): [End-Grain-Calc-mac.dmg](https://github.com/timhanley/end-grain-calc/releases/latest/download/End-Grain-Calc-mac.dmg)
- **Windows** (10 or 11): [End-Grain-Calc-windows.exe](https://github.com/timhanley/end-grain-calc/releases/latest/download/End-Grain-Calc-windows.exe)

Those two links always fetch the newest version. The app tells you when a
newer one is out with a small button in its header.

## Opening it the first time

The apps are free and are not signed with a paid Apple or Microsoft
certificate, so your computer asks you to allow them once.

**Mac.** Open the disk image and drag End Grain Calc into Applications, then
open it. macOS says it can't check the app: click Done. Open System Settings,
go to Privacy & Security, scroll down to the line about End Grain Calc and
click Open Anyway, then confirm. From then on it opens like any other app.

**Windows.** Save the .exe wherever you like and double-click it. If Windows
shows "Windows protected your PC", click More info, then Run anyway. The
window is drawn by Microsoft's WebView2, which comes with Windows 11 and is
on almost every Windows 10 computer; if it is missing, the app says so and
where to get it.

Your boards and settings are kept in a folder called `.endgrain` in your home
folder, so a new version picks up where the last one left off.

## Check the numbers

Check the numbers before you buy timber or cut it. End Grain Calc is a free
tool and it can be wrong, and your saw, your timber and your mill will not
match its assumptions exactly. It comes with no warranty, and the author takes
no responsibility for errors or for anything that follows from using it. See
the [licence](https://github.com/timhanley/end-grain-calc/blob/main/LICENSE).
